reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that all perceived reality is a mathematical isomorphism of raw sensation, meaning the structure of our experience mirrors the structure of our inputs exactly. This implies that no new information is created during perception; we merely impose a smoother, more ordered framework on the same chaotic data. For the blind, this ordering process relies heavily on synthesis (sequential building) rather than analysis (holistic deduction), leading to a fundamentally different cognitive map. Even sighted individuals operate similarly when dealing with scales beyond direct observation, relying on symbolic multiplication of local impressions to infer global properties. The primitives formalize these concepts: the "Perceptual Order Isomorphism" captures the smoothing operation, the "Sensation Identical to Order" states that no information is lost, "Blind Space Construction" models the sequential synthesis approach, and "Symbolic Perception" explains how high-level symbols can preserve key functional effects. These operators are structurally unified under the universal lens because they all describe different facets of how complex sensory data is transformed into actionable cognitive structures.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage traces back to Kant's transcendental idealism, which posited that space and time are forms of intuition rather than inherent properties of things-in-themselves. This was later formalized mathematically by Poincaré's conventionalism and Hilbert's axiomatization of geometry. The modern computational neuroscience view of hierarchical predictive coding shares the core idea that perception is an active process of constructing consistent models from bottom-up sensory data.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: An agent who believes they perceive reality directly (rather than through an isomorphic filter) may overestimate their certainty and underestimate the influence of prior expectations. Conversely, an agent aware of the isomorphism may better calibrate their confidence by recognizing that their mental model is just one possible reconstruction among many equally valid ones.
